title: optimize-quant-kernels-int8-fp8-smoothquant-dequant-fusion-kvcache-batching-scheduling
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Context: This PR addresses several performance bottlenecks observed in quantized inference (INT8 and experimental FP8) running in the Redwood serving runtime. Recent internal perf runs and customer canaries showed suboptimal throughput for short-to-medium sequence lengths when smoothquant and dequant fusion paths were enabled, and we observed increased stalls when KV-cache population interacted with continuous batching. Motivation: Improve end-to-end token throughput and tail latency while preserving numerical parity for common LLMs (7B-70B-class) when using INT8/FP8 quantization and smoothquant preprocessing. Scope: 1) introduce a fused dequant->matmul kernel path that avoids an intermediate full-precision reorder and reduces memory traffic, 2) optimize INT8/FP8 kernel paths for coalesced loads and register tiling on NVIDIA Ampere/Blackwell GPUs, 3) add scheduler heuristics to prefer KV-cache warm workers for continuous batching and to maintain small-batch latency SLOs, 4) introduce a lightweight KV-cache prefetch hint to reduce first-inference stalls when streaming continuous batches. Summary of changes: fused dequant+gemm kernel with optional smoothquant scaling baked into the kernel; codepaths guarded by runtime capability checks (hw, compute capability, model shape); new scheduler policy hook that biases batching choices based on KV-cache hit-rate and recent latency, and a prefetch hint API for transports to indicate likely warm keys. Tests: microbenchmarks, model end-to-end throughput tests, unit tests for numeric equivalence (within margin), and a staged canary on Dedicated where feature flag was toggled. Results: typical improvements of +18% throughput on INT8 (A100, seq=128, batch auto) and median +12% tail latency reduction for streaming workloads. Risk: changes are guarded behind runtime feature flags and a deploy-time canary rollout to mitigate regressions. Rollout: rolled out via canary to 5% of Dedicated capacity, monitored for perf regressions for 72 hours, then ramped to 50% before global merge. Linear/Jira: references ENG-4321 (kernel perf), ENG-4410 (scheduler), SUP-88 (customer support triage).

perf(quant): optimize INT8/FP8 memory layout and register tiling for matmul kernels
scheduling: add kvcache-aware batching policy and warm-worker bias hook
transport: add kvcache prefetch hint and unit tests
tests: add numeric equivalence checks and microbenchmarks
ci: update performance CI to include new benchmark baselines

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Please add a fallback path for older GPUs without tensor cores; responded with a runtime capability check and unit test.
Priya Nair: Numeric parity looks good for INT8 but FP8 had a small regression on extreme prompts; added tighter unit tests and clamped scaling in the FP8 path.
Ethan Liu: Can we avoid increased memory churn during warmup? Added KV-cache prefetch hint and warm-worker bias to reduce thrash.
Aisha Kapoor (author): Addressed comments, added tests, and rolled a canary. Perf CI initially failed but subsequent fixes passed.
ci_checks: perf-regression: fail -> root cause: FP8 scaling bug in initial kernel; fixed -> rerun -> pass
merge_outcome: merged via squash after staged canary and perf CI green
release_notes: - Improved INT8/FP8 fused kernels with smoothquant & dequant fusion resulting in ~+18% throughput on typical workloads. - Scheduler now favors KV-cache-warm workers for continuous batching, reducing tail latency by ~12% on streaming workloads. - New transport prefetch hint to reduce first-token stalls when KV-cache is empty.
risk_and_rollout: Feature gated behind runtime flags. Deployed as a canary to 5% Dedicated capacity for 72h, observed metrics, ramped to 50% then global. Rollback is a toggle flip at the control plane to disable fused kernels and scheduler hook.
perf_results: INT8 (A100, seq=128, auto-batch): baseline 450k tokens/s -> new 531k tokens/s (+18%)
FP8 experimental (A100, seq=128): baseline 470k tokens/s -> new 540k tokens/s (+15%)
KV-cache warmup 1st-token latency: baseline 85ms -> new 40ms (via prefetch hint)
